summary_en: The Shimizu Bank revised its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027, raising the interim and full-year dividend per share by 5 yen each to 35 yen and 70 yen respectively, from the previous forecast of 30 yen and 60 yen. The increase reflects upside to earnings from higher interest rates on lending and securities income.
title_en: Notice on Revision of Earnings Forecast and Revision of Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
The Shimizu Bank raised its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The interim dividend per share was increased by 5 yen to 35 yen, and the full-year dividend was raised by 5 yen to 70 yen, compared with the prior forecast of 30 yen interim and 60 yen full year.

The company cited stronger than anticipated operating results driven by higher interest rates. Net interest income and securities dividends exceeded the initial forecast as rates rose, benefiting the bank's funding operations. The company also revised upward its full-year earnings forecast, with consolidated net profit attributable to the parent company increasing from 250.0 billion yen to 290.0 billion yen.

According to the bank's shareholder return policy, it maintains a base stable dividend of 60 yen and aims toward a dividend payout ratio of approximately 30% on a progressive basis, while ensuring sufficient capital buffers to support sound management and smooth credit supply to customers.
